questions.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation $T$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 & 9 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Find $a+b+c,$ given that the matrix form of the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ -1 & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix form of $T$ gives us the following information:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}8 & 9 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 8-9\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}5 & -9 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}5 & -9 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=\frac{5}{4}+(-\frac{9}{4})+2=1.
$$

questions.problem:
The affine transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=2-u-v,\,y=3u+4v-1.
$$

Given that the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ of $T$ is

$$
u=7+ax-y,\,v=bx+y+c,
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

So, writing our transformation in matrix form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2-u-v \\ 3u+4v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u-v \\ 3u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{4\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-2 \\ y+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4\cdot (x-2)+(-1)\cdot (y+1) \\ 3\cdot (x-2)+1\cdot (y+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7-4x-y \\ 3x+y-5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ in coordinate form is

$$
u=7+(-4)x-y,\,v=3x+y+(-5).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-4+3+(-5)=-6.
$$

questions.problem:
The affine transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=u-v-1,\,y=3v-2u-6.
$$

Given that the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ of $T$ is

$$
u=ax+y+9,\,v=bx+y+c,
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

So, writing our transformation in matrix form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v-1 \\ 3v-2u-6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ -2u+3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x+1 \\ y+6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3\cdot (x+1)+1\cdot (y+6) \\ 2\cdot (x+1)+1\cdot (y+6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3x+y+9 \\ 2x+y+8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ in coordinate form is

$$
u=3x+y+9,\,v=2x+y+8.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=3+2+8=13.
$$

Consider the affine transformation $T,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What would be the image of the square shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any affine transformation 

$$
T:u⟶Au+b,
$$

where $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix and $u$ and $b$ are $2\times 1$ column vectors, we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $T$ is non-singular, i.e., when $det(A)\ne 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $T$ is singular, i.e., when $det(A)=0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $A$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $A$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a point on the plane.

With that in mind, let's examine our transformation.

Notice that the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}].$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-3)-6\cdot 1 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a singular nonzero matrix. 

Therefore, $T$ is non-invertible and the image of the square under the action of $T$ is a line segment.
